title: HarborView Diagnostics private deploy cutover playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working cutover playbook and module notes for HarborView Diagnostics' private deployment (VPC + on-prem GPU racks). Target audience: solutions-eng, infra SRE, customer ops.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Customer wants an initial 3-node (A100) inference cluster inside their AWS account with a private control plane proxy back to Redwood.
- Need predictable 99th percentile latency < 250ms for 512-token requests, and nightly autoscaling to handle batch jobs for offline processing.
- Proposed phased plan: preflight (net & IAM), pilot (2-week shadow), staged cutover (canary traffic -> route all), post-cutover stabilization.

Key assumptions (call these out in the proposal):
- HarborView will provide a dedicated VPC with two private subnets (az-a, az-b) and a transit gateway peering for on-prem traffic.
- Customer agrees to allow a small set of egress IPs for the Redwood control proxy (list in linked_artifacts).
- KMS keys will be managed by HarborView; Redwood will be granted decrypt/encrypt usage for model artifacts during install.
- Initial model load: Llama-3-70B quantized to 4-bit (we will provide quantization profile), requires ~160GB GPU RAM per replica.
- Expected steady QPS: 20 rps (conversational), burst to 60 rps. Average tokens per request: 180.

Sizing recommendations and rationale:
- GPU tier: 3 x A100 (80GB) in a single capacity group to allow KV cache sharing with minimal model sharding. Rationale: 2x would be fragile for rolling upgrades; 4x is over budget for pilot.
- CPU nodes: 3 x m5.4x for control-plane agents + data plane sidecars (pull model artifacts, run health checks).
- Disk/provisioning: each GPU node 2TB NVMe (local) for model shards and cache; EBS snap backup to S3 for artifacts.
- Network: ENA enhanced networking + at least 25 Gbps between nodes to keep inter-GPU synchronization latency low.
- Memory: 512GB host RAM per GPU node to support large KV caches and batching.
- Headroom: reserve 20% capacity for background maintenance and canaries.

Traffic shaping and capacity plan:
- Continuous batching turned on for queries < 75ms arrival windows. Set max_batch_size=48 for latency SLO trade-offs.
- Nightly offline batch window 02:00-05:00 where we will allow model warmers and heavier quant pipelines.
- Autoscaling policy: scale out threshold at 70% GPU util sustained 2m; scale in below 40% for 5m. Use conservative cooldowns during pilot.

Terraform module notes (practical patterns and TODOs):
- Module layout: modules/
  - network/ (vpc, subnets, route-tables)
  - iaas/ (asg, launch-templates, instance-profile)
  - control-proxy/ (proxy helm chart values, security groups)
  - stateful/ (model-artifact, s3-buckets, lifecycle)
  - kms-integration/ (grant policies, key-alias wiring)
- Remote state: use Terraform Cloud workspace per customer (recommended) OR S3 backend with DynamoDB lock if customer cannot use TFC. State key: harborview-prod-v1.
- Secrets: avoid raw secrets in tfvars; use KMS-encrypted tfvars and an external secrets provider (Vault).
- Upgrade strategy encoded in modules: feature-flagged instance_profile_name and autoscaling_group_min to support canary node pools.
- Important variables: allowed_control_ips (list), model_shard_size_gb, gpu_instance_type, batch_window_ms, kv_cache_mb. Keep sane defaults in variables.tf and mark customer-specific overrides in a separate tfvars file.
- Module outputs: control_proxy_endpoint, node_pool_names, iam_role_arns. Keep outputs minimal and stable across module versions.

State migration and compatibility notes (upgrade plan):
- We are refactoring the asg -> eks (nodegroup) conversion in a later release; for this customer keep ASG approach to minimize surface area. Newer installs can be ported using terraform state mv for resource renames.
- Before any resource replacement, snapshot EBS volumes and record AMI IDs. Maintain a pre-upgrade checklist in the repo.
- Rolling upgrade pattern: cordon -> drain -> replace (1 node at a time). Maintain at least N-1 nodes up at all times.
- If changing model bits (e.g., quant type), use a blue/green variant: deploy variant B on dedicated lane, shadow 10% traffic for 48 hours, then flip route.

Networking and security (open questions for HarborView):
- Do we have a transit gateway or direct connect for on-prem access? (affects egress IPs and routing).
- Which KMS CMKs are available for use and who holds key admin privileges?
- Firewall rules: do their internal firewalls allow the ephemeral ports used by Redis/KV sync (TCP 6379-like ports)?
- SSH / Bastion policy for SRE access during pilot? We recommend ephemeral session manager or jumpbox with short-lived certs.

Rollback and failure modes (high-level playbook):
- Failure during canary: immediate divert traffic to hosted Redwood API fallback. If model crashed but nodes healthy, revert to prior model artifact via s3 snapshot and restart agent.
- Failure during in-place node replacement: bring up replacement node in parallel, warm model, then remove old node. If network partition detected, fail-safe to offline queueing mode.
- Total rollback: restore pre-cutover Terraform state snapshot and trigger route reversion in the control plane.

Operational runbook (first 30 days):
- Day -14 to -1: preflight checklist (IAM, VPC peering, KMS grants, test S3 and snapshot access).
- Week 0 (pilot): deploy infra, load model artifacts in staging lane, run synthetic latency load tests, validate telemetry.
- Week 1-2 (shadow): mirror 5% production traffic, iterate on batching settings, tune batch_window_ms and max_batch_size.
- Week 3 (canary): start routing 20% production traffic to private cluster with auto-fallback.
- Week 4 (full): 100% routing and monitoring for 72h intensive check.

Telemetry and SLOs to verify (metrics):
- 95th/99th percentile token latency per model (target < 250ms at 512 tokens).
- Token throughput (tokens/s) per GPU and overall cluster throughput.
- Errors per 10k requests and fallback frequency.
- Cost estimation: pilot monthly run-rate (infra + data egress): estimate $XXk/month (placeholder to finalize after instance family confirmation).

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: quantized model OOM on certain token patterns. Mitigation: enable per-request token cap and KV cache trimming during peak.
- Risk: Terraform state desync across teams. Mitigation: single owner for remote state + TFC locks and runbook for emergency state restore.
- Risk: Network egress blocked by customer's firewall updates. Mitigation: preflight egress test and include static IP allowlist change window in rollback plan.

Action items (owner initials):
- AP: create pilot Terraform workspace and seed variables (due 2025-01-15).
- DR: validate KMS grant flow with HarborView security (due 2025-01-12).
- NC: run synthetic load test harness against staging (due 2025-01-20).
- EM: draft customer-facing cutover runbook and rollback checklist (due 2025-01-18).

Notes / discussion fragments (raw):
- "If they insist on EKS, we should map ASG names to nodegroup names and provide a simple migration helper script."
- "Consider smaller initial model (13B quant) if customer cannot commit to 3x A100 — reduces latency headroom but faster ramp."
- "We should add an optional module to enable amber-alerts (critical-loss routing) that flips to hosted API if private cluster falls below 1 node."

Appendix: quick Terraform checklist for customer handoff:
- Ensure remote state backend configured and lockable.
- Provide an ops account with kms:Decrypt & s3:GetObject for model artifacts.
- Confirm list of allowed_control_ips for control proxy and open required ports.
- Provide AMI baseline or allow our golden AMI build process during pilot.

End of WIP playbook. This doc is intentionally conversational — will iterate into a final customer proposal after the preflight call on 2025-01-10.
